keyFindings.description: Under forced colors (Windows High Contrast) the appearance:none box shows a ticked and an unticked item the same: the browser forces the fill to the system background and keeps the url() tick, whose fixed colour (white in light, slate-900 in dark) then matches that background. Seen in Chromium with emulateMedia forcedColors 'active' in light and dark (throwaway probe of the head's CSS rules); adding '@media (forced-colors: active) { .dispatch-markdown [data-markdown-task-checkbox] { appearance: auto } }' made the native box draw a visible tick in the same probe. This is the issue's own defect for high-contrast readers.

Lines 471 and 481 put two hand-written colours (%23ffffff, %230f172b) inside percent-encoded SVG data URIs. styles-css-pin.test.ts's exhaustiveness pattern /#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b|rgb\(...\)/ does not see '%23', so the colours skip the pin gate that packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md (styles-css-pin.test.ts paragraph) and the test's own comment say every hand-written colour must pass.
Line 535 pointer-events: none lost its explaining clause in 89bf76b8; every other unusual declaration in the block is explained.
The ticked/unticked/disabled/list-style assertions repeat between the two rows, and the iphone Thread-dialog ternary now has three copies (task-items, theme, held-sends). Cleanup only.
